sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Longitudinal grayscale endovaginal US shows a complex right ovarian cyst with thin, echogenic, lace-like internal echoes , representing fibrin strands. Note subtle posterior acoustic enhancement .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-01

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Longitudinal Doppler US shows an avascular complex right ovarian cyst containing thin, echogenic reticular echoes , signifying an HOC. The surrounding ovarian parenchyma displaced along the periphery of the HOC (claw sign) shows internal blood flow with venous waveform .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-02

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Longitudinal grayscale transvaginal US shows complex pelvic fluid with diffuse low-level echoes along the left aspect of the cul-de-sac, signifying hemoperitoneum related to a left HOC (not shown).
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-03

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Clinical photograph during laparoscopy shows blood in the cul-de-sac behind the uterus secondary to a ruptured hemorrhagic ovarian cyst. Blood clot is seen adherent to the ovarian capsule.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-04

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: In the adnexa of the same patient, an HCL with thick wall and peripheral blood flow is seen on this color Doppler US. This should not be mistaken for the ring of fire associated with tubal ectopic pregnancies. With HCL, the cyst is clearly within the ovarian parenchyma.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-05

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Transverse transabdominal US shows bilateral enlarged ovaries "kissing" posterior to the uterus in this patient who recently stopped birth control pills. Both ovaries contain cysts with echoes .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-06

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Longitudinal grayscale US in a patient with a hemorrhagic cyst and complex pelvic fluid (not shown) demonstrates extension of fluid into the hepatorenal fossa , signifying moderate to large hemoperitoneum.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-07

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT shows high-attenuation fluid in the upper abdomen, specifically the perihepatic space and hepatorenal fossa , representing large volume hemoperitoneum secondary to an HOC in the pelvis (not shown).
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-08

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Coronal CECT shows large hemoperitoneum secondary to a right ovarian HOC. Active bleeding can be seen in the right adnexal region . High-density fluid signifying blood extends into the upper abdomen, including the right paracolic gutter , hepatorenal fossa , and perisplenic region .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-09

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial T1WI FS MR shows that the mass remains high signal, indicating that it does not contain fat and must therefore contain blood products as the source of high signal.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: RP-10

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Transvaginal color Doppler US shows a hemorrhagic cyst with diffuse, increased echogenicity resembling a mature cystic teratoma. Follow-up US revealed complete resolution.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-01

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Transvaginal color Doppler US shows an avascular hemorrhagic cyst with fibrin strands creating a reticular pattern described as lace-like, fishnet, or cobweb appearance. Septations are incomplete in contrast to septations within ovarian neoplasms.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-02

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Transvaginal color Doppler US shows a hemorrhagic cyst with a fine reticular meshwork of fibrin strands and a straight edge along the retracting clot .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-03

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Transvaginal color Doppler US shows a hemorrhagic cyst with a retracted avascular clot .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-04

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Transvaginal color Doppler US shows a fishnet appearance, a common appearance of hemorrhagic cyst.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-05

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Transvaginal color Doppler US shows a hemorrhagic corpus luteal cyst in a pregnant woman with pelvic pain. It is filled with low-level echoes and has peripheral increased vascularity, "ring of fire" . This can be confused with an ectopic pregnancy, but most ectopics are located in the fallopian tube and can be separated from the ovary by exerting gentle pressure with the probe.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-06

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial T1WI MR shows an intermediate to slightly high signal intensity right ovarian cystic mass .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-07

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial T1WI FS MR should always be performed, as it increases lesion conspicuity and rules out a fat-containing lesion. Hemorrhagic cysts are quite variable in signal intensity, reflecting both the age and concentration of blood products.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-08

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial T2WI MR in the same patient shows that the lesion remains high signal.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-09

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Transvaginal US in the same patient shows low-level echoes with a slight reticular pattern typical of a hemorrhagic cyst . Note the posterior acoustic enhancement . In the reproductive age group, hemorrhagic cysts with a classic appearance do not require follow-up unless > 5 cm.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-10

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Color Doppler US shows a classic fishnet appearance created by fibrinous strands . In addition, there is a retracting clot adherent to the cyst wall.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-11

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Transvaginal US shows a typical case of a hemorrhagic cyst with fibrinous strands and a retracting clot .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-12

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial T1WI MR shows a predominately hypointense left ovarian cyst with a vague, hyperintense fluid-fluid level posteriorly . While the classic teaching is that hemorrhagic cysts are hyperintense on T1WI, they are actually quite variable, with many being hypointense, the result of a small amount of hemorrhage in a relatively larger amount of fluid within the cyst.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-13

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial T1WI C+ MR shows enhancement of the thin surrounding cyst wall but no enhancement of internal components.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-14

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial T2WI MR in the same patient best shows the fluid-fluid level with a separation of the clot from the larger serous component.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-15

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Sagittal transvaginal US in the same patient shows the smooth edge of the retracting clot .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-16

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial T2WI MR shows the low-signal clot to better advantage. This is another appearance of hemorrhage on MR. A follow-up US was performed in this case. The clot had retracted with near-complete involution of the cyst by 6 weeks.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-18

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Transvaginal color Doppler US in a 29-year-old woman who presented with acute pelvic pain shows an avascular adnexal structure , representing a hemorrhagic cyst. The margins of the ovary are obscured, and there is variable echogenicity, ill-defined material within the pelvis , representing clotted and unclotted blood.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-19

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Transvaginal Doppler US in the same patient shows variable echogenicity, ill-defined material surrounding the uterus and within the cul-de-sac due to hemoperitoneum.
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-20

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT in a 38-year-old woman who presented with acute pelvic pain shows a ruptured, collapsed hemorrhagic right ovarian cyst with surrounding high-attenuation free fluid . Note higher attenuation of fluid around the ovary compared to fluid away from it (sentinel clot sign).
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-21

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Axial CECT in a 25-year-old woman who presented with acute pelvic pain shows a ruptured hemorrhagic left ovarian cyst with surrounding high-attenuation free fluid . Note the defect in the cyst wall .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-22

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Sagittal transvaginal US of a hemorrhagic cyst demonstrates a hypoechoic mass with low-level and linear echoes (fishnet appearance) .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-23

sourceQualifiedImages.caption: Sagittal endovaginal US shows retracting clot sign. Note the straight margin of the clot .
sourceQualifiedImages.label: SDX-24

downloadSentinel:
Completed the full autonomous build for Liver Mass With Central or Eccentric Scar.

Core Validation Pathway A passed using the uploaded Core Radiology, Second Edition, Gastrointestinal Imaging → Liver. Relevant coverage spans approximately GI 105–122, with the central-scar pattern explicitly summarized on GI 119: FNH, fibrolamellar HCC, and giant hemangioma. The surrounding Core sections provide the additional HCC, adenoma, metastasis, cholangiocarcinoma, epithelioid hemangioendothelioma, and Budd-Chiari/regenerative-nodule discriminators used in the synthesis.

The final deck contains 40 cards / 40 TSV lines: 9 Primary UNKNOWNs covering all 9 atomic STATdx teaching clusters and all 24 selected primary images, 6 Mechanism cards, 5 Boards Trap cards, 4 Epidemiology High-Yield cards, and 16 other High-Yield cards. Differential Drill and Definition sections were correctly omitted because they were not explicitly requested. The 22-column audit, unique Clinical_Context-code audit, trigger-isolation audit, blank Tags-column audit, summary-identity audit, Section A cardinality audit, and supplied-caption verbatim audit all passed.

The supplied STATdx URLs could not be authenticated/downloaded from this runtime, so I did not falsely claim that the image binaries were retrieved. The TSV instead preserves the exact source-qualified SDX-##_STATdx_plain_...jpg / SDX-##_STATdx_annotated_...jpg references and the supplied captions.
